claims.value: Angelica Kauffmann (1802); Cardinal Fesch; 1845 auction; Aducci; Vatican 1856
claims.statement: The Vatican catalogue records the panel in the collection of Angelica Kauffmann in 1802 (the earliest attribution to Leonardo is in her will, per the Vatican press release), its reassembly by Cardinal Joseph Fesch after it had been sawn into pieces, its sale after Fesch's death at auction at Palazzo Ricci, Rome, in 1845 to the lawyer Alessandro Aducci, and its purchase for the Vatican on 5 September 1856 at the Monte di Pietà.

background.text: Saint Jerome in the Wilderness is an unfinished painting by the Italian Renaissance artist Leonardo da Vinci, dated c. 1480, 1490. A recent study linked to the Lady with an Ermine carried out by Leonardo da Vinci at the same time supports this hypothesis. The composition of the painting has been drafted in monochrome onto the primed wooden panel. At an unknown date after Leonardo's death, the panel was cut into five pieces before eventually being restored into its original form.
Il San Girolamo penitente è un dipinto a olio su tavola (103×75 cm) di Leonardo da Vinci, databile al 1480 circa e conservato nella Pinacoteca Vaticana. Si tratta di un dipinto non portato a termine.
Saint Jérôme est un tableau de Léonard de Vinci. Ce tableau ne fut jamais achevé, mais est daté approximativement de 1482.
